Source: http://www.seattletimes.com/

Posted February 16, 2000

From the Seattle Times
February 13, 2000
opinion@seatimes.com
http://www.seattletimes.com/
Seattle Times Editorial

ANXIOUS? TRY OREGON
(MarijuanaNews note: An editor? Try the facts!)
Voters in both Washington and Oregon in late 1998 legalized medicinal marijuana for certain painful diseases. Today, Washington's neighbor is considering dramatically expanding the legal reasons for lighting up, including anxiety, sleep disorders and depression.
See
Oregon Medical Marijuana Law May Cover More Ailments

Whoa, dude.
(MarijuanaNews note: Whoa, hack! It’s medical marijuana. Ha ha! Are they incapable of writing on the subject without being terminally cute?)
See
Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Felt Betrayed When Magic Johnson Made A Joke About Him Using Medical Marijuana.

As long as marijuana is considered an illegal drug, better to limit its medicinal use to the current standard: to treat intractable pain unrelieved by standard medical care.
(MarijuanaNews note: Depression can be a form of " intractable pain unrelieved by standard medical care. " There are millions of Americans on pharmaceutical anti-depressants. The drugs work for some people, but for others they either do not work or cause serious side effects. Depression can even be fatal – via suicide – or by undermining a person's health. Sleep disorders can also be very debilitating. Perhaps if the editors were to stay up late informing themselves, they might have better empathy.)
See
DEAland Children Consume 90% of the World’s Ritalin.
" This year six million children across the USA -- over one tenth of the schoolage population --
will be prescribed anti-depressants and stimulants. "
Context for The Medical Marijuana Debate and " Drug Education "
and numerous links

Here in Washington, people with cancer, HIV, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, glaucoma and a few other debilitating dieases can seek a doctor's prescription to possess and use the drug. Oregon's current law has similar standards.

Some patients in both states want to expand the accepted uses.
(MarijuanaNews note: Notice that this is something that the patients want. Why would they want it if pharmaceuticals worked? Well, perhaps they might also want them because some of the " legal " drugs are very expensive and they cannot afford them.)
Washington recently added Crohn's disease to its list of approved diseases. Oregon created an advisory group to study patients' requests to add post-traumatic stress disorder, Alzheimer's disease, anxiety, bipolar disorder, insomnia and other conditions.

The law will keep evolving as the body of medical research grows. The American Cancer Society, for example, agreed last month to fund a three-year study testing a " marijuana patch, " similar to a nicotine patch, that could deliver the drug without the risk of lung disease.
(MarijuanaNews note: Okay, but so what? It will be years before the patch is available, if ever. Also this is for one of the most recognized uses of medical marijuana, treating chemo-related nausea. Cancer patients seldom use enough marijuana to pose any risk to their lungs, even if one grants the most extreme claims about marijuana smoke damaging the lungs. Also, by using vaporizers, already available, this risk can be avoided now. In short, these people don’t have a clue.)
See
Prohibitionist Organization Has Money To Burn On Press Release About How It Is Politically Incorrect To Refer To A " Marijuana " Transdermal Patch

Broadening the list of ailments too quickly could threaten research's progress and funding nationwide. Best to stay focused on the people whose suffering made the medicinal-marijuana law sensible in the first place.
(MarijuanaNews note: What research? In any case, the purpose of medicine is to relieve suffering, not to create opportunities for research!)

See
Perhaps The Single Most Damning Article On Medical Marijuana Fiasco I Have Ever Read – Without Intending To Be
and
Chairman of the House of Lords Science and Technology Committee
Criticizes UK Government’s Rejection Of Report On Medical Marijuana
– 2 Articles With 2 of the Worst Prohibitionist Arguments
